title: The day-30 shelf–Gulf cooling contrast was uncertain in 12 paired Atlantic storms from 1988 to 2024
abstract: We tested a reported difference in sea surface temperature recovery between the US East shelf and the Gulf of Mexico. We reused saved buoy curves and control estimates from a signed campaign study. Twelve storms had usable encounters in both regions, with 47 encounters in 12 years from 1988 to 2024. With equal storm weights, the day-30 shelf-minus-Gulf contrast was -0.377 degrees C. Its 95% year bootstrap interval was -0.926 to +0.180 degrees C. The late contrast minus the early contrast was -0.752 degrees C, with interval -1.558 to +0.028. Selection checks retained negative day-30 means, but all intervals included zero. In the paired sample, the shelf late mean was near its control level and Gulf water was warmer than its controls. This small selected sample does not establish a regional difference or equal recovery. Local forcing, control uncertainty and repeated sensors limit inference. Code, aggregate results, a figure and verified external-input retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Paired shelf-minus-Gulf SST contrasts and selection checks. Bars show pointwise 95% year bootstrap intervals.

citations.reason: Fixed source curves, controls and metadata; new within-storm comparison.
Fixed-sample robustness test left storm and region differences unresolved.
